Container.Name: kb-service
Container.Overview: The one door to the shared knowledge library. It stores items and their vectors in Postgres and serves the /v1 library routes, including the ingest-job routes the ingest worker calls, behind bearer tokens. /v1/chat/completions forwards to the model router. STARTED IN ORDER: kb-postgres, then kb-redis, then kb-litellm, then kb-service, then kb-webui. There is no template equivalent of compose depends_on, so nothing enforces that for you. NETWORK: the kb containers share one user-defined Docker network named kb that you create once, by hand, before the first start (a template cannot create a network, so Network stays bridge here - set it to kb when you create the container). Docker must preserve user-defined networks across updates (Unraid: Settings > Docker, Preserve user defined networks = Yes), or the containers fall back to bridge and the container names stop resolving. EXPOSURE: this container is exposed on your LAN through the host port you choose, behind bearer tokens; anything further (a domain, reverse proxy, TLS) is a separate step for whoever administers your network. MIGRATIONS: when KB_DATABASE_URL is set, the service applies its database migrations at every start. LIBRARY: the /v1 library routes answer 503 until KB_DATABASE_URL and KB_EMBED_BASE_URL are both set; /health answers without a token. REQUIRED: the service refuses to start (exit code 2) without KB_PERSONA_TOKENS, a JSON object of caller name to token with every token at least 32 characters. STORAGE: this release writes nothing to /assets or /export; give each a pool path, and back /assets up once a release writes originals there. The process runs as user 99:100. IMAGE TAG: pinned to one release; an Update is a deliberate bump of that pin.
Container.Description: Knowledge service for the shared library. Start after kb-litellm, before kb-webui. LAN-exposed; set a free host port, the caller tokens and the database URL.

Config.Name: HTTP Port
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Host port for the service (REST at /, MCP at /mcp, health at /health); the container always listens on 8000 internally - change the host side only. No default is offered: pick a free port.

Config.Name: Assets
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Original files and derived images; losing this loses the originals. Set an absolute path on a POOL, e.g. /mnt/<pool>/appdata/kb-service/assets. Put it under backup.

Config.Name: Export
Config.Description: REQUIRED. The nightly plain-file export of the library. Set an absolute path on a POOL, e.g. /mnt/<pool>/appdata/kb-service/export.

Config.Name: Drop
Config.Description: Optional. A share a person drops fund notice PDFs into (set KB_FUND_INBOX=/drop), e.g. /mnt/<pool>/<drop-share>. Files kb reads move out of it; nothing else is written there except a .problem.txt beside a file it cannot read.

Config.Name: KB_PERSONA_TOKENS
Config.Description: REQUIRED. JSON object of caller name to bearer token, format {"<caller>":"<token>"}. Every token is at least 32 characters, no two callers share one, and the object is not empty; otherwise the service exits 2 at start. Use long random values.

Config.Name: KB_FUND_READER_PERSONAS
Config.Description: Comma-separated persona names that may only read the published fund datasets (versions lists, distributions, Form 8937); every other route answers 403. Blank: none.

Config.Name: KB_ADMIN_PERSONAS
Config.Description: Comma-separated persona names with administrator rights: they approve tags and vocabulary and may call POST /v1/admin/reembed. Leave the default unless your admin persona is named otherwise. Blank makes no persona an administrator.

Config.Name: KB_DATABASE_URL
Config.Description: REQUIRED. PostgreSQL connection URL, format postgresql://<user>:<password>@kb-postgres:5432/<db> - the user, password and database set on kb-postgres, the host being its container name on the kb network. Percent-encode any reserved character in the password. The service runs its database migrations when it starts. Blank: the library endpoints answer 503.

Config.Name: KB_MCP_URL
Config.Description: Public https address of the kb MCP endpoint (/mcp) and its OAuth sign-in (/oauth), as Network Admin publishes it. The OAuth issuer and the addresses Claude is sent to are built from it, so it must match the public hostname exactly. Must start with https://; anything else makes the service exit 2. Blank turns the MCP endpoint off.

Config.Name: KB_ROLES
Config.Default: {"PM": "pm", "System Admin": "system-admin", "Network Admin": "network-admin", "Backup Admin": "backup-admin", "Media Admin": "media-admin", "Game Dev": "game-dev", "KB Analyst": "kb-analyst", "Financial Analyst": "financial-analyst", "Travel Planner": "travel-planner"}
Config.Description: The messaging roles kb-mcp delivers between, as JSON: role name exactly as the INBOX.md registry spells it, to the kb persona that role signs in as. One persona per role. Update it when a role is registered or retired. Blank turns messaging off; malformed JSON makes the service exit 2.

Container.Config: {"PM": "pm", "System Admin": "system-admin", "Network Admin": "network-admin", "Backup Admin": "backup-admin", "Media Admin": "media-admin", "Game Dev": "game-dev", "KB Analyst": "kb-analyst", "Financial Analyst": "financial-analyst", "Travel Planner": "travel-planner"}

Config.Name: KB_PROJECTS
Config.Description: Which kb personas belong to which project, for project documents kept in the kb (doc_* tools on kb-mcp), as JSON: project name to members (persona names) and shared (true: every persona may read; false: members only). Members read and write. Add a project when its documents move into the kb. Blank turns project documents off; malformed JSON makes the service exit 2.

Config.Name: KB_STACK
Config.Description: Which library this service fronts. Only global is accepted; any other value makes the service exit 2 at start. Leave global.

Config.Name: KB_EMBED_BASE_URL
Config.Description: Embedding endpoint: the kb-litellm route on the kb network, which serves the embed model. Blank: the library endpoints answer 503, because storing and searching both need embeddings.

Config.Name: KB_EMBED_MODEL
Config.Description: Embedding model name as kb-litellm lists it: the alias, not the model file. Leave embed unless kb-litellm lists it differently. Blank: the service uses qwen3-embedding:0.6b.

Config.Name: KB_EMBED_API_KEY
Config.Description: Key for the embedding endpoint above, sent as its bearer token. Blank if the endpoint takes none.

Config.Name: LITELLM_URL
Config.Description: Base URL of the model router: the kb-litellm container on the kb network. Leave the default. Blank: the chat route answers 503.

Config.Name: LITELLM_KEY
Config.Description: Key for kb-litellm: its master key, or a virtual key it issued. Sent as the bearer token on every call to the router.

Config.Name: KB_WATCHDOG_PING_URL
Config.Description: healthchecks.io ping URL of the kb watchdog's check (from the vault). Every 5 minutes the watchdog pings it while the ingest queue, source re-listing, kb-litellm and embeddings are healthy, and sends /fail with the problems otherwise; any change in problems is also messaged to KB Analyst. Blank turns the watchdog off.

Config.Name: KB_WATCH_OLLAMA_URL
Config.Description: Base address of a desktop Ollama (for example http://<your-pc>:11434) that the watchdog reports on: unreachable, or a model loaded on CPU only. Advisory only: it is messaged to KB Analyst and never fails the healthchecks ping, since the PC may be off. Blank leaves the PC unwatched.

Config.Name: KB_FUND_MODEL
Config.Description: Router model group (kb-litellm) for the second, independent read of fund distribution notices (Shared kb doc KB_Fund_Datasets.md). Public documents only. Blank means claude-haiku.

Config.Name: KB_FETCH_CONTACT
Config.Description: Contact mailbox named in the fund fetcher's User-Agent (SEC EDGAR asks automated readers for one). Set per host; blank sends no address.

Config.Name: KB_FUND_INBOX
Config.Description: Folder inside the container that a person drops fund notice PDFs into, one flat folder (the Drop path below, so /drop). kb-service watches it every 30 s while idle and reads each PDF with the reader of the sponsor it names; a read file moves to KB_FUND_KEEP, a file it cannot read stays with a .problem.txt beside it. Blank turns the drop folder off.

Config.Name: KB_FUND_KEEP
Config.Description: Folder inside the container where read fund notices are kept, one flat folder, each renamed <sponsor>_<period>_<tickers>_<sha8>.pdf. They are the evidence behind published rows: keep it under /assets (backed up). Blank means /assets/fund_notices.

Config.Name: KB_EXPORT_DIR
Config.Description: Container path the export is written to. Nothing in the pinned release reads it yet. Leave /export: it is the mount above.

Config.Name: KB_ASSETS_DIR
Config.Description: Container path original files and derived images are stored under. Nothing in the pinned release reads it yet. Leave /assets: it is the mount above.
